repositories.prompt_note: Multica is an agent orchestration platform. Service areas: `area:backend-go` (Go server, pgx, database), `area:frontend-next` (Next.js views/packages), `area:daemon` (agent dispatcher, KUBECONFIG injection, task dispatch), `area:runtime` (Docker/K8s runtime, lue-kube deploy), `area:docs` (markdown docs, README). Use at most two area tags. When the item spans multiple areas, use `area:cross-cutting`. Validation: `cd server && go test ./...` for backend; `pnpm check` for frontend/packages.

Core AI is the backend AI/agent service for CLIP-SA. Service areas: `area:api` (REST/GraphQL endpoints), `area:ai-engine` (model routing, completions, tool dispatch), `area:auth` (authentication, session, permissions), `area:integrations` (OpenClaw, external service connectors), `area:infra` (Docker, CI, env config). Use at most two area tags. When the item spans multiple areas, use `area:cross-cutting`. Validation: use the repo's primary test and lint commands.

Core Wholesale is a multi-stack ecommerce platform. Service areas: `area:next-frontend` (Next.js storefront, React components, pages), `area:woocommerce` (WooCommerce plugin customisations, hooks, REST API extensions), `area:wordpress` (WordPress core customisations, themes, ACF, plugin integrations), `area:mysql` (database schema, queries, migrations, performance), `area:openclaw-integration` (OpenClaw agent/AI integration, tool dispatch, session management). Use at most two area tags. When the item spans multiple areas, use `area:cross-cutting`. Validation: appropriate per area — PHP unit tests for WP/WC, `pnpm build` for Next.js, SQL migration checks for MySQL.

Pi is Luke's fork of the Pi agent toolkit (coding agent CLI, unified LLM API, TUI/web UI libraries, Slack bot, vLLM pods). The local checkout lives at `~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork/`; the GitHub repo is `valkyriweb/pi-mono`. Service areas: `area:coding-agent` (the agent harness, session, tools, executor, context), `area:extensions` (dream-memory, pi-memory, claude-bridge, and other extension packages), `area:tui` (terminal UI, themes, keybindings, components), `area:sdk` (SDK integrations, custom providers, model additions), `area:docs` (markdown docs, examples, prompt templates), `area:tests` (unit and integration tests). Use at most two area tags. When the item spans multiple areas, use `area:cross-cutting`. Validation: `pnpm --filter coding-agent test` for harness changes; `pnpm -r build` for the monorepo. Default review provider stays Codex; Claude-bridge routing is opt-in per slice 7.

ClawSweeper is the GitHub issue/PR triage and repair automation in this repository. Service areas: `area:workflow` (GitHub Actions, tokens, permissions, dispatch), `area:repair` (issue intake, worker planning/execution, post-flight merge), `area:github-api` (gh/REST/GraphQL calls, search, permissions), `area:validation` (target validation command parsing), `area:tests` (unit and repair tests). Use at most two area tags. When fixing workflow bugs, prefer surgical changes with regression tests and validate with `pnpm run check` or the narrowest repair test/build gate.

Luke's patched fork of OpenClaw (agent gateway). Tracks upstream openclaw/openclaw with carry-forward patches tracked in ~/Projects/infra/openclaw-claude/docs/issues.md (ISSUE-040, ISSUE-042, ISSUE-077, ISSUE-091, ISSUE-094, ISSUE-095, cron-list-fix). Service areas: `area:agent-runtime` (ACP, agent loop, session lifecycle), `area:tools` (bash/exec, image_generate, web, sessions_*), `area:plugins` (advisor, context-intelligence, pi-ai), `area:bridge` (claude-bridge sidecar), `area:tests` (vitest). Use at most two area tags. When the item spans multiple areas, use `area:cross-cutting`. Validation: `pnpm exec vitest run <test-file>`. **CRITICAL: do NOT propose closing carry-forward PRs as 'implemented on main' — these are upstream-bound patches, not yet merged upstream.** Carry-forward PRs are typically named with `carry(<version>):` prefix; treat them as long-lived.

K3s cluster repo for client workloads (Laravel, WordPress, OpenClaw). Areas: `area:apps` (k3s/apps/<name>/{base,overlays/prod}), `area:flux` (Flux CD reconciliation), `area:cluster` (cluster-level config, system add-ons, sealed-secrets), `area:secrets`, `area:docs`. Use at most two area tags. Validation: `kubectl --context lue-kube` for cluster-side checks; manifests don't ship without `flux reconcile`. Carry-forward PRs do not exist here.

OpenClaw management hub for Luke's production OpenClaw runtime: release notes, update logs, live-runtime issues, methodology, Paperclip wiring, plans, state, and docs. Mostly markdown; no source build. Areas: `area:release-risk`, `area:runtime-k8s`, `area:pi-harness`, `area:bridge-cache`, `area:skills-extensions`, `area:telemetry-evals`, `area:media-audio`, `area:context-health`, `area:docs-cleanup`, `area:methodology`. Use at most two area tags. Review as an ops/release triage assistant, not a generic stale-docs cleaner. Important work: read linked release logs/changelogs completely, compare against Luke's active runtime/cluster surfaces, and flag stability fixes, breaking config changes, Docker/Kubernetes/runtime impacts, prompt-cache/context health, Pi harness/bridge changes, skills/extensions, TTS/STT/media, heartbeats, telemetry/tracing/Opik/evals, active-memory, smoke/staging/build-test needs, and CHANGELOG/release tracking updates. Treat `docs/releases.md`, `docs/agent-context/update-release-runbook.md`, `state/update-log.jsonl`, `memory/MEMORY.md`, and `docs/issues.md` as operational state, not stale clutter. Prefer `manual_review` for release audits, runtime decisions, workflow design, plans, state logs, pending methodology, or anything needing cluster/operator judgment. Use `queue_fix_pr` only for narrow docs/index/changelog cleanup with an obvious existing file and no product/runtime decision; if no scoped validation command exists, choose `manual_review`. Do not propose closing methodology TODOs, pending-work notes, active plans, issue tracker entries, or release records as stale. Close only clear duplicates, cannot-reproduce reports, or items outside this repo boundary.
